need: A repeated async /run request from the same caller returns the first job's id instead of starting a second paid run.

searched.found: Jobs are an in-memory dict with a TTL and lock; nothing looks a job up by request. Catalog runs already reject a stale expected_checkpoint_id but only after a second run starts.
no listed capability covers request deduplication
A client-sent Idempotency-Key header; the server stores the first response per key and replays it, and errors are replayed only when processing began.

candidates.name: Idempotency-Key header (IETF draft, as used by Stripe)
candidates.covers: Replays the first response for a repeated request.
candidates.misses: Needs every client, including the page, to send a key; today none does, so protection would be absent for the requests that matter.
candidates.reason: Same semantics are kept, but the key is derived server-side from caller and body so no client change is needed.

candidates.name: Server-derived request hash with in-memory job lookup
candidates.covers: Protects every client with no change to them, inside the existing job table.
candidates.misses: Lost on restart (running jobs also end then).
candidates.reason: Smallest change that closes the gap; adds no engine or scheduler capability.
